regions.name: flow_far_wake
regions.why: The far-wake requirement volume is also uncovered (coverage 0.0). Level 2 gives h = 0.375/2^2 = 0.09375 m, under the required 0.175 m span cap, and is deliberately one level coarser than the near wake to bound cost of the slowly recovering deficit, matching the stated mechanism that far-wake transport is coarsenable. It is the same size as the existing 0.28125 m distance shell, so the wake box merges without a stair-step.

regions.name: flow_aft_shear_core
regions.why: Mechanism, not score-chasing: the dimensionless estimate discharges an aft-body boundary layer of about 0.0489 m, which is only ~1.04 level-3 cells (0.046875 m), so the emerging shear layer and velocity-deficit edge behind the trailing edge would be smeared over a single cell. Level 4 halves the cell to 0.0234375 m (~2 cells across the estimated discharge thickness) in the first 1.0 m of wake, where the cross-stream gradient is steepest, while leaving the rest of the near wake at level 3 and the far wake at 2. Lateral extent is kept identical to the near-wake box so the shear layer is not clipped by a lateral refinement boundary; the only level change is a single 4->3 step in streamwise direction, within n_cells_between_levels = 3. Level 4 is within +2 of the global surface level 3. This is a hypothesis-driven resolution increase expected to matter only for the near-field deficit; it is not evidence that the wake is accurately resolved.

regions.name: repair_0
regions.why: actual layer deficit concentrated in measured boundary faces

regions.name: flow_near_wake
regions.why: Keep the wake requirement volumes compliant under the restored spec by re-asserting the near-wake corridor at level 3. Level 3 gives 0.375/2^3 = 0.046875 m, matching the measured native near-wake max span 0.0472 m against the 0.0875 m cap, so this is a no-regression guard rather than an increase. Far-wake level 2 (0.09375 m) is explicitly NOT re-declared or refined: its measured native max span 0.0943 m is already 1.86x under the 0.175 m cap, and spending 8x cells there would only shrink the attempt budget that the measured layer repair needs. Bounds match flow_requirement:near_wake exactly so no new level jump is introduced.

advisor.hypothesis:
The residual failure is NOT a bulk layer-count deficit: round1 already extruded 8468/8584 body faces (98.65%). The shortfall is a LOCAL defect. Round0 used 8 layers and reached only 0.33% coverage; round1 used 7 layers and reached 89.83% coverage with 86.7% of area at exactly 7 layers. So extrusion is all-or-nothing per face. The failing faces carry 0-4 layers, and layer_shortfall:0 / layer_shortfall:1 show why: they are the blunt fore/aft bands (x≈-1.59..-1.13 and x≈1.13..1.59) where solid normal half-thickness is only ~0.195-0.254 m and the measured median local feature is ~0.43 m, while the requested stack is 0.0160 m. Native log shows the medial-axis mover is NOT thickness-truncating ("Reducing layer thickness at 0 nodes"), and it reports "isolated points extrusion stopped : 4" plus "Disabled extrusion at" on 3 ranks. This is a corner/edge extrusion-suppression regime, not an out-of-space regime: the extrusion direction changes rapidly there (dihedral p95 8.6 deg is fine, but curvature proxy p95 8.95 normal-rotation/m and thickness/medial proximity at the polar cap), so neighbouring face normals collide and the driver zeroes the whole column. Remaining 11.7% of area is at 0-4 layers, dominated by 0-layer (2.37%) and 1-4 layer bands on exactly those two caps.

Mechanism hypothesis: the polar/aft band columns are stopped by the interaction of (a) featureAngle 60 with the tessellated cap curvature, which suppresses extrusion near surface "features" that are really smooth curvature, and (b) normal smoothing being too weak (n_smooth_surface_normals 1, n_smooth_normals 3) to produce a coherent extrusion direction across the cap, plus medial-axis angle 90 being restrictive for a blunt body whose fluid medial distance from the cap is comparable to the local feature. Fix the cap extrusion regime, not the global cell size: raising global level or adding wake boxes cannot fill suppressed faces.

Note the y+ gate is intact: first_height 0.0012379 m gives estimated y+ p50 50.0 exactly, so first height must NOT be touched (no sane flow field exists; no wall-shear evidence, so wall_height is inadmissible). The layer stack already fits by 27x, so n_surface_layers can go back to 8 (round0's own value) at no geometric risk.

Counterevidence to alternatives: (1) More wake/local refinement (round1's repair_0 at level 4 over the body) did not fix layers - coverage stayed under 90%; resolution is not the lever. (2) Switching mesh_shrinker is not indicated: one ablation counterexample (torus) shows changer-alone leaves 1.74% coverage, and the native medial mover is already the better-documented path with quality passing (max_non_ortho 57.6 vs gate 65, n_failed 0). (3) n_grow is explicitly propagation of NON-extrusion; it would shrink coverage, not fill faces, so it stays 0. (4) nOuterIter is a layer partition, not a retry counter; a 2-outer split is used only as a measured-safe change in construction order, not as a remedy assertion.
advisor.expected_change: Area fraction with >=5 actual layers should rise from 0.8983 to >=0.90 (acceptance threshold). Concretely: the 0-layer band (2.37% of area) and the 1-4 layer bands (7.60% of area) on the two blunt cap bands (layer_shortfall:0, layer_shortfall:1) are expected to redistribute upward as feature_angle is raised to 150 (round1's surface features already use included_angle 150; the layer feature_angle 60 is far tighter than the tessellation's own feature threshold) and normal smoothing increases (n_smooth_surface_normals 1->4, n_smooth_normals 3->10). Quality must remain verified: max_non_ortho should stay below 65, n_failed 0, min_volume > 1e-13, and fidelity must stay accepted (bidirectional p99 is 0.00126 m vs 0.015 m tolerance, so ample margin). Off-body native spans (near 0.0472 m vs 0.0875 cap; far 0.0943 m vs 0.175 cap) must not regress. Uncertainty: I cannot predict the exact recovered coverage, and if the caps are limited by genuine native fluid medial distance rather than by angle/normal smoothing, coverage may improve only partially; in that case a targeted local surface refinement at the two caps would be the next intervention, not a global level change. Cell count should stay near 325k (single attempt budget 2e6, attempt 1 already 325k).
alternatives: Add a level-4 local_refine box on the two cap bands (x -1.6..-1.1 and 1.1..1.6) so more faces subdivide the cap curvature - rejected for now because resolution was already increased in round1 (repair_0, surface level 3 plus level-4 near wake) without crossing 90%, so a resolution-only mechanism lacks a new causal reason and would add cost without addressing extrusion suppression.

Switch mesh_shrinker to displacementMotionSolver - rejected because the native medial-axis mover already shows zero thickness truncation and verified quality, and the only evidence for the motion solver is a synthetic ablation that on a torus left 1.74% coverage; changing one knob alone is not a general repair.
Raise n_grow to 1-3 - rejected on documented semantics: nGrow propagates NON-EXTRUSION to neighbours and zeroes displacement, so it can only reduce covered area.

Restore round0 anchor (8 layers, 166k cells) and modify from there - considered; round1 is the better anchor because it is the measured-valid native-quality/fidelity candidate with the far higher coverage (0.898 vs 0.003) and cells 325k << 2e6 budget.

Keep 7 layers - rejected because with all-or-nothing extrusion a taller stack does not reduce suppression, and round0's 8-layer anchor shows 8 is feasible; 8 also adds a safety margin for the >=5-layer gate on faces that currently land at 4.

Increase surface_level globally to level 4 - rejected: initial_certification already shows finest 0.046875 with unresolved_feature_fraction 0.0, so there is no unresolved-geometry evidence to justify doubling surface cost.
counterevidence: layers.coverage 0.8983 is below the 0.9 required_area_fraction, but 86.73% of area sits at exactly 7 layers (vs requested 7), i.e. most of the body is fully extruded - the deficit is a 11.7% local cohort, not a global thickness/layer deficit.

Native layer log: 'Reducing layer thickness at 0 nodes where thickness to medial axis distance is large' and 'Written 0 points with too large an extrusion distance' - the medial-axis clamp (max_thickness_to_medial_ratio) is NOT the active limiter, so relaxing medial ratios is not the evidenced lever.

Native layer log nevertheless shows extrusion disabled on ranks 6, 14, 15 and 'Number of isolated points extrusion stopped : 4' - a local, corner-like suppression cohort exists, consistent with layer_shortfall clusters concentrated on the two blunt cap bands.

layer_shortfall:0 and :1 report finite_fluid_gap_fraction 0.0 and null fluid_gap/p95 outward ray distance - five directional rays found no finite outward hit, so these clusters do not prove a narrow true fluid gap; the blocker is extrusion direction/angle, not available space, and the requested 0.0160 m stack is tiny versus median local feature ~0.43 m.
Round1 added the level-4 near-wake and body-covering region (repair_0) and cells rose 166k -> 325k without reaching 90% layer coverage - more cells were not the mechanism.
flow_probe is absent and rans_grade is 'unverified'; actual y+ is unavailable, so no first-height or wall_height change can be justified and the current estimated y+ p50 = 50.0 must be preserved.

Quality is already verified/accepted (max_non_ortho 57.57 < 65, max_skew 0.703 < 4, n_failed 0), so layer repair must not trade away quality by aggressive corner handling; slip_feature_angle is left at 30 and the extrusion-stop mechanism is addressed with angle/smoothing rather than shrinker replacement.

The candidate anchor is provisional ('no industrial accuracy certificate') and remaining_mesh_attempts is 3 - restore must be first, and adjacent-cap boxes must be optional fallbacks, not stacked into one plan.
